definition: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the biological material that carries the instructions for making proteins that help build the body’s cells. It is inherited from biological parents, and small differences in DNA between people can contribute to differences in appearance, personality, health, and vulnerability to mental disorders.

reasons: The claim that differences in DNA can contribute to vulnerability to mental disorders is not directly supported by the packet; it says certain genes, along with biological and environmental factors, can be associated with mental disorders.
The definition goes beyond the packet by turning a general association with mental disorders into a stronger causal claim about individual vulnerability.

The definition claims that DNA differences contribute to “vulnerability to mental disorders,” but the packet only states that certain genes can be associated with mental disorders; it does not support the specific idea of “vulnerability.”

The definition is otherwise broadly consistent with the packet’s supported claims (genes as DNA segments forming proteins; inheritance from biological parents; variations contributing to differences in appearance/personality/health; associations with mental disorders).
